days.quip: A whole queen?! Misha, you beautiful maniac.
days.caption:
TAL WEEK — Day 1 of 7 🧙

Mikhail Tal vs Vasily Smyslov, Candidates 1959.

22-year-old Tal faces the legendary Smyslov — and hurls his QUEEN at f7. Smyslov grabs it. A few moves later his position is in ruins. This brilliancy-prize game carried Tal all the way to the World Championship.

A new Tal classic every day this week — follow so you don't miss Day 2.

days.caption:
TAL WEEK — Day 2 of 7 🧙

Bobotsov vs Tal, Varna 1958.

The night before this game, Tal played blitz for hours — the SAME queen sacrifice, over and over, while everyone giggled. Next day Bobotsov played 11.Nd5... and Tal took the knight without blinking, leaving his queen hanging. Two pieces and a raging attack beat the queen.

Day 3 tomorrow: Tal takes on the World Champion himself.

days.caption:
TAL WEEK — Day 3 of 7 🧙

Botvinnik vs Tal, World Championship 1960, Game 6.

Against the most scientific player who ever lived, 23-year-old Tal threw a knight into empty air: 21...Nf4!! Nobody could prove it was sound — but at the board, in the chaos, Botvinnik couldn't cope. Tal won the game, then the match, and became the youngest World Champion in history.

TAL WEEK — Day 4 of 7 🧙

Tal vs Tringov, Amsterdam Interzonal 1964.

Tringov grabbed a poisoned pawn and went queen-hunting. Tal let him have the whole queenside — his pieces only cared about one square: f7. Bishop sac, knight check, queen crash. Tringov resigned on move 17 with mate on the board next move.

Day 5 tomorrow: Tal leaves his queen hanging and just… keeps playing.

days.caption:
TAL WEEK — Day 5 of 7 🧙

Tal vs Hecht, Varna Olympiad 1962.

Hecht attacked Tal's queen and expected a retreat. Instead: 19.exf6!! — Tal simply left the queen hanging and took a knight with a pawn. By the time the dust settled he had three minor pieces and total control for it. He squeezed out the win 30 moves later.

days.caption:
TAL WEEK — Day 6 of 7 🧙

Tal vs Larsen, Candidates Semifinal 1965, the deciding Game 10.

Earlier in this game Tal hurled a knight into the center with 16.Nd5!! — a sacrifice analysts argued about for decades. Larsen defended brilliantly for 34 moves. Then came Re8+, Qe6+, and the quiet killer Qf7. Mate cannot be stopped. Tal won the game and the match.

Tomorrow's finale: Tal vs a 16-year-old named Bobby Fischer.

days.caption:
TAL WEEK — Day 7 of 7 🧙

Tal vs Fischer, Candidates 1959.

Tal went 4–0 against 16-year-old Bobby Fischer in this tournament — this is the most famous of those wins. Fischer grabbed pawns; Tal built a storm, crashed through with Ne6+, and Fischer resigned facing mate. Fischer never forgot it — he put a loss to Tal in his '60 Memorable Games'.
